content_list.content_text: In the wake of the 2001 terrorist attacks, there were visible signs of soul-searching in American cinema. Spike Lee (b. 1957) responded with the heartfelt 25th Hour (2002). The film, which revolves around the last day of freedom of a man about to be sent to prison, is a love letter to Lee's beloved New York as well as a study of consequences and responsibility.

information.contentText: Adapted by David Benioff from his own novel The 25th Hour, it tells the story of a man's last 24 hours of freedom as he prepares to go to prison for seven years for drug dealing.

content_list.content_text: Dramatized reconstructions of what happened on September 11 were dominated by Paul Greengrass's (b. 1955) harrowing United 93 (2006). Oliver Stone's (b. 1946) World Trade Center (2006) drew criticism from all sides. Stone was also criticized for his biopic of George W. Bush, W. (2008). Although it was far from the devastating indictment some had hoped for, Stone's aim was to pose a more ambitious challenge to a system that allowed a man like him to reach the Oval Office.

quote.quote: I'd like to dedicate this Oscar to the women and men in the military who risk their lives on a daily basis.
quote.author: Kathryn Bigelow on The Hurt Locker

content_list.content_text: The subsequent conflicts in Afghanistan and Iraq were addressed in a variety of films, but despite the presence of big stars, Syriana (2005), Good Night, and Good Luck. (2005) - a clever allusion to the McCarthy witch hunt that reflected the Bush administration's "you're either with us or against us" rhetoric - Home of the Brave (2006), In the Valley of Elah (2007), Grace Is Gone (2007), and Stop-Loss (2008) failed to attract a wider audience.

information.contentText: The film is about a village whose inhabitants live in fear of creatures that inhabit the woods beyond it. Like other films written and directed by Shyamalan from the same period, The Village has a twist ending.

content_list.content_text: The Oscar-winning The Hurt Locker (2008) could be read as an endorsement of either left- or right-wing positions on the conflict in Iraq. Ridley Scott (b. 1937) contributed Body of Lies (2008), an old-school thriller updated to explore the CIA's current dealings overseas, while David Cronenberg (b. 1943) reminded 2005 audiences of the homegrown "at home" depravity and the darkness lurking in everyday life in the elegant A History of Violence (2005).

Steven Spielberg's (b. 1946) blockbusters such as Minority Report (2002) and War of the Worlds (2005) - whose apocalyptic opening scenes recall Manhattan just after the planes hit - were no longer so different from his more "serious" works. If A.I. Artificial Intelligence (2001) divided audiences and critics over its quality, the debate surrounding Munich (2005) took place in the political arena.

information.contentTitle: Scenes from There Will Be Blood
information.contentText: Anderson, who had already said he would like to work with Daniel Day-Lewis, wrote the screenplay with Day-Lewis in mind and approached the actor when the script was nearly complete. Anderson had heard that Daniel Day-Lewis liked his previous film, Punch-Drunk Love, which gave him the confidence he needed to hand Day-Lewis a copy of the unfinished screenplay. According to Day-Lewis, knowing the part had been written with him in mind was what convinced him to take it on.

content_list.content_text: Dissatisfaction with the film's message stirred up both pro- and anti-Israel factions at the same time. Nevertheless, Spielberg and screenwriter Tony Kushner's (b. 1956) take on the Mossad agents who hunt down those responsible for the massacre at the 1972 Olympics is powerful. The film raises questions about retaliation and draws parallels with the attack on the Twin Towers and the American government's response.

quote.quote: In this day and age, 2005, I can't understand why anyone would question any actor playing a gay role.
quote.author: Heath Ledger on Brokeback Mountain

content_list.content_text: In the aftermath of 9/11, filmmakers found themselves looking to the past, to American history, and to the roots of the national psyche. Paul Thomas Anderson (b. 1970) directed There Will Be Blood (2007) and conveyed the message that many contemporary films explored during the Bush administration - that power corrupts and breeds paranoia and fear in those who benefit from it. With Gangs of New York (2002) and The Aviator (2004), Martin Scorsese (b. 1942) examined the birth of the modern United States - capitalism, racial tensions, and, in the characters of the brutal Bill the Butcher and the unstable millionaire Howard Hughes, the dangers of greed and isolationism.

movies.overview: Ruthless silver miner, turned oil prospector, Daniel Plainview, moves to oil-rich California. Using his son to project a trustworthy, family-man image, Plainview cons local landowners into selling him their valuable properties for a pittance. However, local preacher Eli Sunday suspects Plainview's motives and intentions, starting a slow-burning feud that threatens both their lives.
movies.title: There Will Be Blood

movies.overview: Forced to play a dangerous game of cat-and-mouse in the chaos of war, an elite Army bomb squad unit must come together in a city where everyone is a potential enemy and every object could be a deadly bomb.
movies.title: The Hurt Locker

movies.overview: In New York City in the days following the events of 9/11, Monty Brogan is a convicted drug dealer about to start a seven-year prison sentence, and his final hours of freedom are devoted to hanging out with his closest buddies and trying to prepare his girlfriend for his extended absence.
movies.title: 25th Hour

movies.overview: During the 1972 Olympic Games in Munich, eleven Israeli athletes are taken hostage and murdered by a Palestinian terrorist group known as Black September. In retaliation, the Israeli government recruits a group of Mossad agents to track down and execute those responsible for the attack.
movies.title: Munich

movies.overview: It's 1863. America was born in the streets. Amsterdam Vallon returns to the Five Points of America to seek vengeance against the psychotic gangland kingpin, Bill the Butcher, who murdered his father years earlier. With an eager pickpocket by his side and a whole new army, Vallon fights his way to seek vengeance on the Butcher and restore peace in the area.
movies.title: Gangs of New York

movies.overview: John Anderton is a top 'Precrime' cop in the late-21st century, when technology can predict crimes before they're committed. But Anderton becomes the quarry when another investigator targets him for a murder charge.
movies.title: Minority Report

movies.overview: An average family is thrust into the spotlight after the father commits a seemingly self-defense murder at his diner.
movies.title: A History of Violence

movies.overview: An attorney is trying to solve her younger brother's mysterious disappearance while simultaneously helping a new friend rid herself of a stalker. As she begins to uncover the truth, it turns out that the seemingly separate situations are actually connected.
movies.title: Personal Effects

movies.overview: When a willful young man tries to venture beyond his sequestered Pennsylvania hamlet, his actions set off a chain of chilling incidents that will alter the community forever.
movies.title: The Village

movies.overview: A real time account of the events on United Flight 93, one of the planes hijacked on 9/11 that crashed near Shanksville, Pennsylvania when passengers foiled the terrorist plot.
movies.title: United 93

movies.overview: The story of the eventful life of George W. Bush—his struggles and triumphs, how he found both his wife and his faith—and the critical days leading up to his decision to invade Iraq.
movies.title: W.
